column1: Chelsea Rochman, an ecologist at the University of California, Davis, has been trying to answer a dismal question: Is everything terrible, or are things just very, very bad?
column2: 加州大学戴维斯分校的生态学家切尔西·罗赫曼一直在试图回答一个令人沮丧的问题：究竟是一切都糟透了，还是情况只是非常、非常糟？
column4: University of California, Davis|加州大学戴维斯分校

column1: Rochman is a member of the National Center for Ecological Analysis and Synthesis’s marine-debris working group, a collection of scientists who study, among other things, the growing problem of marine debris, also known as ocean trash.
column2: 罗赫曼是美国国家生态分析与综合中心海洋废弃物工作组的成员。组内科学家的研究对象之一，就是日益严重的海洋废弃物问题，也就是我们常说的海洋垃圾。
column4: marine-debris|adj. 海洋废弃物方面的
column7: among other things|除了研究其他事物以外

column1: Plenty of studies have sounded alarm bells about the state of marine debris; in a recent paper published in the journal Ecology, Rochman and her colleagues set out to determine how many of those perceived risks are real.
column2: 许多研究都已就海洋废弃物的现状敲响警钟。罗赫曼和同事在最近发表于《生态学》期刊的一篇论文中，着手查明这些被认为存在的风险中有多少确实存在。
column8: set out to determine|着手查明
column9: perceived risks|被认为存在的风险

column1: Often, Rochman says, scientists will end a paper by speculating about the broader impacts of what they’ve found.
column2: 罗赫曼说，科学家往往会在论文结尾推测，自己已有的发现可能产生哪些更广泛的影响。

column1: For example, a study could show that certain seabirds eat plastic bags, and go on to warn that whole bird populations are at risk of dying out.
column2: 例如，一项研究可能发现某些海鸟会吃塑料袋，随后便警告说，整个鸟类种群都面临消亡的风险。
column5: go on to warn|接着提出警告
column6: whole bird populations|整个鸟类种群

column1: ‘But the truth was that nobody had yet tested those perceived threats,’ Rochman says.
column2: “但当时的实情是，还没有人检验过这些被认为存在的威胁。”罗赫曼说。
column4: nobody had yet tested|尚无人检验过
column5: perceived threats|被认为存在的威胁

column1: ‘There wasn’t a lot of information.’
column2: “手头的信息并不多。”
column3: There wasn’t a lot of|并没有多少

column1: Rochman and her colleagues examined more than a hundred papers on the impacts of marine debris that were published through 2013.
column2: 罗赫曼和同事们审查了截至2013年已发表的一百多篇有关海洋废弃物影响的论文。
column6: impacts of marine debris|海洋废弃物的影响

column1: Within each paper, they asked what threats scientists had studied — 366 perceived threats in all — and what they’d actually found.
column2: 他们逐篇追问，科学家研究了哪些威胁，实际又发现了什么。这些论文提及的潜在威胁共有366项。
column3: Within each paper|在每一篇论文中
column5: perceived threats|被认为存在的威胁

column1: In 83 percent of cases, the perceived dangers of ocean trash were proven true.
column2: 在83%的案例中，人们所担心的海洋垃圾危害得到了证实。
column5: perceived dangers|人们认为存在的危险

column1: In the remaining cases, the working group found the studies had weaknesses in design and content which affected the validity of their conclusions — they lacked a control group, for example, or used faulty statistics.
column2: 在其余案例中，工作组发现研究的设计和内容存在缺陷，影响了结论的有效性，例如没有设置对照组，或者使用了有问题的统计方法。
column9: faulty statistics|有问题的统计方法

column1: Strikingly, Rochman says, only one well-designed study failed to find the effect it was looking for, an investigation of mussels ingesting microscopic plastic bits.
column2: 罗赫曼说，值得注意的是，设计严谨却没有发现预期效应的研究只有一项，考察的是贻贝摄入微小塑料碎片后会怎样。
column9: microscopic plastic bits|微小的塑料碎片

column1: The plastic moved from the mussels’ stomachs to their bloodstreams, scientists found, and stayed there for weeks — but didn’t seem to stress out the shellfish.
column2: 科学家发现，塑料从贻贝的胃进入其血液循环，并在那里停留数周，却似乎没有让这些贝类出现应激反应。

column1: While mussels may be fine eating trash, though, the analysis also gave a clearer picture of the many ways that ocean debris is bothersome.
column2: 不过，贻贝吃了垃圾也许没有明显不适，这项分析却也让人们更清楚地看到了海洋废弃物带来危害的多种方式。

column1: Within the studies they looked at, most of the proven threats came from plastic debris, rather than other materials like metal or wood.
column2: 在他们审查的研究中，多数得到证实的威胁源于塑料废弃物，而非金属或木头等其他材料。

column1: Most of the dangers also involved large pieces of debris — animals getting entangled in trash, for example, or eating it and severely injuring themselves.
column2: 多数危险还涉及大块垃圾。比如，动物被废弃物缠住，或因吞食废弃物而严重受伤。
column3: Most of the dangers|大部分危险

column1: But a lot of ocean debris is ‘microplastic’, or pieces smaller than five millimeters.
column2: 但海洋废弃物中有许多是“微塑料”，也就是小于5毫米的塑料碎片。

column1: These may be ingredients used in cosmetics and toiletries, fibers shed by synthetic clothing in the wash, or eroded remnants of larger debris.
column2: 这些微塑料可能是化妆品和洗护用品中的成分，也可能是合成纤维衣物在洗涤中脱落的纤维，或较大废弃物磨蚀后留下的碎屑。
column9: eroded remnants|磨蚀后留下的碎屑

column1: Compared to the number of studies investigating large-scale debris, Rochman’s group found little research on the effects of these tiny bits.
column2: 罗赫曼的研究组发现，与研究大块废弃物的众多论文相比，有关这些微小碎片会造成哪些影响的研究很少。

column1: ‘There are a lot of open questions still for microplastic,’ Rochman says, though she notes that more papers on the subject have been published since 2013, the cutoff point for the group’s analysis.
column2: “关于微塑料，还有许多悬而未决的问题。”罗赫曼说。不过她也指出，自研究组分析所覆盖的最后一年2013年以来，这一领域又发表了更多论文。

column1: There are also, she adds, a lot of open questions about the ways that ocean debris can lead to sea-creature death.
column2: 她补充说，关于海洋废弃物究竟通过哪些途径造成海洋生物死亡，同样还有很多问题没有答案。

column1: Many studies have looked at how plastic affects an individual animal, or that animal’s tissues or cells, rather than whole populations.
column2: 许多研究考察的是塑料怎样影响某个动物个体，或其组织和细胞，考察的对象并非整个种群。

column1: And in the lab, scientists often use higher concentrations of plastic than what’s really in the ocean.
column2: 而在实验室里，科学家常用的塑料浓度高于海洋中的实际浓度。

column1: None of that tells us how many birds or fish or sea turtles could die from plastic pollution — or how deaths in one species could affect that animal’s predators, or the rest of the ecosystem.
column2: 这些研究都不能告诉我们，究竟会有多少鸟、鱼或海龟死于塑料污染，也不能告诉我们，一个物种中个体的死亡会怎样影响以它为食的动物，或生态系统的其他部分。
column8: rest of the ecosystem|生态系统的其余部分

column1: ‘We need to be asking more ecologically relevant questions,’ Rochman says.
column2: “我们需要问一些更符合生态实际的问题。”罗赫曼说。
column4: ecologically relevant|与生态实际相关的

column1: Usually, scientists don’t know exactly how disasters such as a tanker accidentally spilling its whole cargo of oil and polluting huge areas of the ocean will affect the environment until after they’ve happened.
column2: 油轮意外泄漏所载的全部原油、使大片海域受到污染，这类灾难究竟会怎样影响环境，科学家通常要到事后才能弄清楚。
column6: whole cargo of oil|船上装载的全部原油

column1: ‘We don’t ask the right questions early enough,’ she says.
column2: “我们没有及早问对问题。”她说。
column3: ask the right questions|问对问题

column1: But if ecologists can understand how the slow-moving effect of ocean trash is damaging ecosystems, they might be able to prevent things from getting worse.
column2: 但如果生态学家能弄清海洋垃圾如何在长期的缓慢作用中损害生态系统，或许就能防止情况继续恶化。

column1: Asking the right questions can help policy makers, and the public, figure out where to focus their attention.
column2: 问对问题，有助于政策制定者和公众弄清应该把注意力集中在哪里。

column1: The problems that look or sound most dramatic may not be the best places to start.
column2: 视觉或听觉上最惊人的问题，未必最值得先着手解决。
column3: look or sound|看起来或听起来

column1: For example, the name of the ‘Great Pacific Garbage Patch’ — a collection of marine debris in the northern Pacific Ocean — might conjure up a vast, floating trash island.
column2: 比如，“大太平洋垃圾带”这个名字指的是北太平洋聚集着的一批海洋废弃物，却可能让人想象出一座广阔的漂浮垃圾岛。
column3: Great Pacific Garbage Patch|大太平洋垃圾带
column4: collection of marine debris|海洋废弃物的聚集体
column8: floating trash island|漂浮的垃圾岛

column1: In reality though, much of the debris is tiny or below the surface; a person could sail through the area without seeing any trash at all.
column2: 可实际上，其中许多垃圾要么十分细小，要么在水面以下。即使乘船穿过这片海域，也可能什么垃圾都看不到。

column1: A Dutch group called ‘The Ocean Cleanup’ is currently working on plans to put mechanical devices in the Pacific Garbage Patch and similar areas to suck up plastic.
column2: 一个名为“海洋清理”的荷兰团体正在拟订方案，准备在太平洋垃圾带及类似海域放置机械装置，把塑料吸走。
column4: The Ocean Cleanup|“海洋清理”组织

column1: But a recent paper used simulations to show that strategically positioning the cleanup devices closer to shore would more effectively reduce pollution over the long term.
column2: 但近期一篇论文通过模拟表明，从长远看，经过谋划将清理装置部署在离海岸更近的地方，能更有效地减轻污染。
column8: over the long term|从长远看

column1: ‘I think clearing up some of these misperceptions is really important,’ Rochman says.
column2: “我认为，澄清其中一些误解非常重要。”罗赫曼说。

column1: Among scientists as well as in the media, she says, ‘A lot of the images about strandings and entanglement and all of that cause the perception that plastic debris is killing everything in the ocean.’
column2: 她说，无论在科学界还是媒体中，“许多动物搁浅、遭到缠绕之类的画面，都使人们以为塑料废弃物正在杀死海里的一切生物”。

column1: Interrogating the existing scientific literature can help ecologists figure out which problems really need addressing, and which ones they’d be better off — like the mussels — absorbing and ignoring.
column2: 仔细审视现有科学文献，可以帮助生态学家判断哪些问题确实需要处理，哪些倒不如像贻贝那样，吸收了也不必理会。
